summary.headline: Arvind Q1 FY27 consolidated revenue rose 25% to INR2,501 crores and EBITDA 39% to INR258 crores, with Dalco-GFT consolidated for about 1.8 months.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue was INR2,501 crores (+25%) and EBITDA INR258 crores (+39%), with EBITDA margin up 104 bps to 10.3%. Excluding Dalco-GFT, revenue grew 17% to INR2,344 crores and EBITDA 26% to INR234 crores. Textile volumes were strong (denim at a 16-quarter high, garmenting above 11 million pieces), but textile EBITDA margin fell to about 8% on raw material inflation that management estimates at about INR100 crores in H1, mainly cotton and yarn plus petrochemical-linked chemicals. Advanced Materials posted record quarterly revenue of INR650 crores and EBITDA of INR97 crores (15% margin). A INR500 crore maiden QIP was completed and is being used for debt reduction.

financial_highlights.change: revenue +13%; textile EBITDA margin about 8% vs 8.4% last year
highest ever quarterly revenue and EBITDA

segments.name: Textile
segments.commentary: Revenue INR1,735 crores (+13% as stated on the call; management said textile revenue grew 21% in an analyst question) with EBITDA INR139 crores; margin about 8% vs 8.4% a year ago. Denim volume 17.5 million meters (+34%, 16-quarter high); woven fabric 31.2 million meters (+7%).

segments.name: Garmenting
segments.commentary: Revenue INR497 crores, with volume up 13% and pieces above 11 million for the first time; revenue growth moderated by a higher mix of value-segment products. Margin about 7.5% per analyst; management expects a double-digit margin only around mid-next year.

segments.name: Advanced Materials India
segments.commentary: Revenue INR493 crores (India business growth about 40%) and EBITDA INR74 crores. Human protection gained from normalised Indian defence procurement and easing US tariff pressure; composites grew about 76% partly on roughly 10% of Q4 orders shifting into Q1; industrial grew more slowly due to capacity constraints.

segments.name: Dalco-GFT (US)
segments.commentary: Contributed revenue INR157 crores and EBITDA INR24 crores (15.1% margin) for about 1.8 months post-acquisition. Full-quarter run-rate was INR244 crores revenue and INR40 crores EBITDA (16.3% margin).

guidance_outlook: Advanced Materials to grow close to 20%; FY27 growth for the India business put at about 18-20% on revenue with EBITDA margin growth above that, and composites normalised at high-teens to 20%.
Dalco-GFT FY27 growth about 9-10% as integration and capex start; mid-teens targeted from next year. Dalco FY27 revenue expected around INR900-1,000 crores (100-110 million units per management).
Garmenting FY27 growth expected close to 15%; medium-term target mid-teens revenue growth; double-digit EBITDA margin expected around mid-next year (about 18-24 months).

Textile margins expected to recover gradually as price increases pass through; timing unpredictable while the conflict continues. Mid-teens to high-teens growth in industrial expected from Q4 as new capex ramps.
Net debt to end the year about INR500 crores below the current level, roughly offsetting the India debt raised for the Dalco acquisition.
capex_capacity: Denim capacity is effectively at 100% utilisation; debottlenecking capex and an asset-light lease model are adding capacity; management did not quantify the denim capacity figure.

Dalco-GFT: upgrades on 2 of 7 lines to come on stream in 3-4 months (capacity from Q4); line 8 decision expected in 1-2 months, adding about 7-8% capacity. Dalco term loan to be repaid over five years.
Garmenting: new Varanasi factory starting next month; 2-3 brownfield factories being debottlenecked via automation and second shifts. Garmenting operating at 100% utilisation.
Industrial (filtration) capex delayed by shipping, execution and flooding; expected to come online this quarter, with disproportionate investment allocated to industrial this year.
Q1 growth capex of about INR98 crores. Advanced Materials India capital employed INR853 crores; Dalco INR326 crores; working capital about 90-100 days in AMD India versus about 50 days at Dalco.
demand_pricing: Order books are filled 3-4 months ahead with prices fixed, so raw material escalations pass through with a lag of a couple of quarters; management said it traded growth for margin to protect market share.

Garmenting: about 50% of denim goes to Bangladesh; new partnership garmenting units in Bangladesh and Egypt, with a target of about 20% of business in the medium term (up to 30% if very successful) at EBITDA margin around high single digits, 2-3 points below own plants.
Europe exports are small today at about 8-10% of group sales; UK design gallery in London opened, with EU FTA expected to take 18-20 months to convert into meaningful business.
Advanced Materials India share and new defence customers expanded across defence and paramilitary; global defence to be pursued over 12-18 months.
Dalco demand outlook: US infrastructure bill supporting geo-textiles; auto leadership to be maintained and US filtration business to be built from the Dalco base.

qa_highlights.question: Why did textile margin decline to about 7.5-8%, and how will it recover over the next two to three quarters?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said Q1 is seasonally weak and textile margin was 8% vs 8.4% a year earlier; it was about 1-1.5 points below potential due to the raw material shock. Price increases are being passed on, with margins expected to improve as pricing catches up.

qa_highlights.question: When will garmenting margins reach low double digits?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said 18-24 months, with new plants at negative margins weighing on the average. Later in the call, it said mid-next year is the expected point for double-digit margins.

qa_highlights.question: Will the garmenting FY27 growth target of about 15% hold?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said it should be close to 15% because denim dispatches with higher ASPs shifted from Q1 into Q2; Q1 was skewed to knits.

qa_highlights.question: What is the expected FY27 combined margin for AMD plus Dalco?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the combined margin will be similar to the 15-17% range; Dalco is at 16-17% and was pressured by petrochemical-linked raw materials, expected to recover to 16-plus% as pricing catches up.

qa_highlights.question: What is the net debt outlook for the full year?
qa_highlights.answer: Net debt will settle about INR500 crores below current levels; the INR450-odd crore US debt is serviced by the US entity, and India debt returns close to pre-Dalco levels.

qa_highlights.question: How should the partnership garmenting model be evaluated on returns and margins?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said return on capital employed will be higher because of low capital employed, with margins 2-3 points below own plants, at high single digits if successful. Management is going conservatively this year.

risks_watch: Raw material inflation (cotton, yarn, petrochemical-linked inputs) with an ongoing Middle East conflict; full pass-through timing is uncertain.
Textile and Dalco margin recovery depends on price catch-up on fixed-price orders placed 3-4 months ahead.
Industrial segment growth lagging because of capex delays; new capacity must come online this quarter for mid-teens to high-teens growth from Q4.
Garmenting new capacity ramp and partnership model execution; new plants can run at negative margins before stabilising.
Working capital intensity rising (AMD India 90-100 days) as the company carries extra raw material stock to protect customer commitments.
summary.management_tone: Confident on volumes and demand and on the order book, but cautious on margins; management attributed the textile margin shortfall to a temporary raw material shock and was guarded on timing, saying the conflict is still ongoing. Answers on the Dalco debt schedule and garmenting margins were more specific.
key_quotes: So we traded growth for margin, you could say.
I would say we are about one and one and a half basis points off because of the overall war impact, and there's nothing more than that.
As I've consistently mentioned that we are in an execution constrained environment rather than a market constrained environment.
So the focus right now is on building the business.

Industrial (filtration) capacity expansion, delayed, expected online this quarter

growth.why: Management guides Advanced Materials FY27 revenue growth high-teens to 20%, Garmenting close to 15%, and Dalco 9-10% (cut, with teens targeted next year); backing is partial: Varanasi factory starting, Dalco line upgrades in 3-4 months, and order books filled 3-4 months ahead, but denim capacity was not quantified.

rows.label: Margin expansion
rows.why: Textile margin fell to about 8% vs 8.4% a year ago on roughly INR100 crore H1 raw material inflation; management expects gradual recovery as price increases pass through on fixed-price orders placed 3-4 months ahead, but timing is unpredictable while the conflict continues.

rows.label: Capacity expansion / commissioning
rows.why: Garmenting Varanasi factory starts next month and garmenting runs at 100% utilisation; Dalco-GFT upgrades on 2 of 7 lines come on stream in 3-4 months (Q4), and line 8 (about 7-8% capacity) is decision-pending in 1-2 months; industrial filtration capacity expected online this quarter.

rows.label: Volume growth
rows.why: Denim volume up 34% to 17.5 million meters at a 16-quarter high with denim capacity effectively at 100%; garmenting pieces above 11 million (+13%) and FY27 garmenting growth guided close to 15%.

rows.label: New capex announcement
rows.why: Denim and garmenting both at 100% utilisation, with Dalco line 8 decision expected in 1-2 months and Q1 growth capex already about INR98 crore; debottlenecking and asset-light leases are the stated routes, so further capex announcements are likely.

rows.label: Guidance upgrade
rows.why: Dalco FY27 growth was cut to 9-10% and textile margins are about 1-1.5 points below potential, so the guidance direction is held or trimmed rather than raised.

rows.label: Guidance downgrade
rows.why: Dalco FY27 growth was cut to 9-10% and textile margin recovery depends on raw material pass-through with the Middle East conflict ongoing; industrial growth lags until capex comes online.

rows.label: New product launch
rows.why: Partnership garmenting units in Bangladesh and Egypt target about 20% of business (up to 30%) at high single-digit margins, and UK design gallery opened, but no specific new product launch date was given.

rows.label: Advanced Materials FY27 growth high-teens to 20%
rows.why: Normalised AMD revenue growth guided at high-teens to 20%, with composites at high-teens to 20% and India business at 18-20%, backed by Q1 AMD revenue of INR650 crore (record) and about 10% of Q4 orders shifting into Q1.

rows.label: Net debt down about INR500 crore by year end
rows.why: Net debt guided to end about INR500 crore below current level, following INR500 crore maiden QIP used for debt reduction, with India debt returning close to pre-Dalco levels.

rows.label: AMD India working capital intensity rising
rows.why: AMD India working capital at 90-100 days vs about 50 days at Dalco, as extra raw material stock is carried to protect customer commitments.

tone.note: Management was confident on denim volumes, the order book and Advanced Materials, but cautious on textile and Dalco margins and guarded on recovery timing while the conflict continues; analysts pressed on garmenting margin timing, Dalco growth and net debt.
